newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Optus says no timetable set for float.
newsitem.headline: Optus says no timetable set for float.

text.p: Telecoms and pay television operator Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Wednesday that there is no timetable set for its share float.
"A float is a matter for the shareholders and as far as I am aware there is no target date," Optus chief executive officer Peter Howell-Davies told reporters.

On Tuesday, Cable & Wireless Plc doubled its stake in Optus to 49 percent after it bought BellSouth Corp's stake in the Australian telephone group. Howell-Davies is a former executive of Cable & Wireless.

"Now that we have got a simplier shareholding structure and a clear understanding from the shareholders and the management for the way forward, that makes our part much easier now to articulate to our own people what strategy we have," Howell-Davies said.
Optus other shareholder is Mayne Nickless Ltd with 24.9 percent. The rest is owned by local institutions.
Howell-Davies said Optus did not plan to raise any further capital before a potential float.

"We already have a line of credit from the Optus Vision banks and the Optus Communications banks. We still have credit that we have not drawn down yet and we also have commitment from shareholders," Howell-Davies said.

The long-awaited float was delayed last year due to litigation by a former shareholder in Optus' pay television arm Optus Vision. Further uncertainty has surrounded the float timing following the recent change in control and management.
Australian telecommunications analysts value Optus at between A$4.1 billion and A$5.3 billion.

Local investors are expected to see several telecom related floats over the next two years including the government's sale of a third of its shareholding in Telstra Corp Ltd. -- Kevin Morrison 61-2 9373-1813
